# One-scale prime-sum bound on the same host

**Pending independent review** (`pending_review`). Full local implication under the assumptions of [B08](../../units/B08.md). Source edition: paper v4, §3.1, p. 19.

Fix a level and its cyclic order $o$, a positive exponent $\varepsilon$, and the real bounds $e_D,e_L,K,c_{HH},e_K,C_E$. At scale $x$ the host satisfies both the explicit-formula input $\mathrm{EAtH}$ and the core lattice input $\mathrm{CoreAtH}$ of this unit. The claims below use the same subgroup, assignment of columns, kept set and discarded character bound.

[B09](../../units/B09.md) · [B10](../../units/B10.md) · [D014](../../units/D014.md) · [D547](../../units/D547.md) · [D548](../../units/D548.md) · [D549](../../units/D549.md) · [D550](../../units/D550.md)

## The one-scale estimate, B08

Fix the level and all the constants of [B08](../../units/B08.md). Take the
maximum of three thresholds. First take the B09 threshold with
$C=\max(e_D+e_L,0)+3$, $c=(3o+1)^{-1}$, $M=4o$, $C_E$ the
explicit-formula constant and $K_o=\sum_{\psi\in\Lambda.\mathrm{KEPT}}|(L'/L)(1,\psi)|$ in the host’s convention at one. Here $|c|\le1$ since
$o\ge0$. Second require
$\log x,\,200(1+K)^2(1+c_{HH})(1+e_K)\le x^\varepsilon$
([D550](../../units/D550.md)). Third require $1+4o\le x^\varepsilon$.
All three thresholds depend only on the fixed constants.

For any host above that threshold with both the explicit-formula and
core packages, write $c'_{HH},e_{\rm Div},e_{\rm Loss}$ for its internal
constants. Its error windows give $K,e_K,c'_{HH},e_{\rm Div},e_{\rm Loss}\ge0$.
Since $c'_{HH}\le c_{HH}$, the same largeness bound holds for $c'_{HH}$.
Also $0\le e_{\rm Div}\le e_D$, $0\le e_{\rm Loss}\le e_L$,
so $C=e_D+e_L+3$. The data have scale $x$ and exponent $\varepsilon$.
The bracket $B$ is nonnegative. Thus B10 and monotonicity of $x^a$
in $a$ give $\mathrm{gap}(u)\le x^{C\varepsilon}B$ for all $u\in A_0$.
The sizes, thinness, costs and containment $T_2\subset A_0$ are fields
of the same core package. D014 supplies its arithmetic host facts and
D548 the required character data. Hence B09 applies.
Using D547 to identify the kept sum and D549 to add the omitted terms,
$$
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal G_\Lambda(x)
   &\le x^{1/2+(e_D+e_L+6)\varepsilon}+4o\,x^{1/2+\varepsilon}\\
   &\le (1+4o)x^{1/2+(e_D+e_L+6)\varepsilon}
    \le x^{1/2+(e_D+e_L+7)\varepsilon}.
\end{aligned}
$$
This establishes B08 for all eligible frames and hosts simultaneously.

`large_x_eventually`, `SubThreeMulLogTwoLe.lean:319–329`.

An admissible host forces the internal division and loss exponents to be nonnegative and bounded above by $e_D,e_L$. This is why a nonnegative exponent can be chosen before existence of a host has been used.

# The finite character average and its four size terms

**Pending independent review** (`pending_review`). Full local implication under the assumptions of [B09](../../units/B09.md). Source edition: paper v4, §3.1, pp. 16–21.

Use the arithmetic host, sizes, width controls and character hypotheses on the B09 statement. Here $a_t$ is the column parameter, $b$ the frozen width, and $w$ its actual local width. The subgroup $A_0$ is averaged uniformly. The identities and estimates for the character data, width and thick-place sum are the separately identified list-A inputs of v4 statements 3.2–3.9 in §3.1.

[D547](../../units/D547.md) · [D548](../../units/D548.md) · [D549](../../units/D549.md) · [D562](../../units/D562.md) · [D561](../../units/D561.md) · [D563](../../units/D563.md) · [B08](../../units/B08.md)

## Which characters are being summed

Put $E_0=(\mathbb Z/2)^2$, $s_0=((1,0),0)$,
$e_1(t)=s_0+(0,t)$ and
$\mathcal A=\{\xi\in\widehat{E_0\times H}:\xi(0,A_0)=1\}$.
The character sum at $y$ is denoted by $G_\xi(y)$.
Write $K'$ for the kept subset, $o=\Lambda.o$, $c=(3o+1)^{-1}$, $M=4o$,
$K_o=\sum_{\psi\in\Lambda.\mathrm{KEPT}}|(L'/L)(1,\psi)|$
with the source's convention for the logarithmic derivative at one.
Define $v_\xi=\mathrm{wt}_c(\xi)\Re G_\xi(x)$ for $\xi\in K'$,
and $v_\xi=-|G_\xi(x)|$ for $\xi\in\mathcal A\setminus K'$.
Here $\mathrm{wt}_c$ is $1$ on the characters trivial on $H$, and $c$
on the other characters. Thus
$G:=\sum_{\xi\in\mathcal A}v_\xi=G_m^A(x)-\Sigma_A(x)$
by splitting the finite sum ([D565 in B09](../../units/B09.md)).

`Deduction.CH.wtA`, `GmA`, `SigA`,
`DedekindLFunctions/SplitInertia.lean:26–40`;
`CharacterBalanceMoves.sum_vv`, `LandauTheorems/ChCore.lean:183–200`.
**Character inputs at the same host.** 
Fix $x>0$. Let the host satisfy the axioms `HostAx` on its frame. Assume $\mathrm{EAtH}(\Lambda,H,TT,x,\varepsilon,C_E)$
and $\ell$ agrees with its primitive-character logarithmic derivatives.
Then $0\in K'\subset\mathcal A$, all kept characters take value one at

$|\sum_{t\in TT}\xi(0,t)-c n_T|\le M x^{-1+\varepsilon}n_T$.

## Conversion to a character lower bound, D564–D565

Use $y_t=a_t/b$, so $|y_t-x|\le1$, and take $x\ge3$.
For nonzero $\xi$, $G_\xi(1)=\ell(\xi)$, whence the increment estimate gives
$|G_\xi(x)|\le x(\log x+C_d+|\ell(\xi)|)$.
For nonzero kept $\xi$, first replace $G_\xi(y_t)$ by $G_\xi(x)$ under
$\sum_t\xi(e_1(t))$. The cost per term is at most
$\log(x+1)+C_d+K_o$. Next replace the sum of its coefficients by
$n_T\mathrm{wt}_c(\xi)$: the values at $e_1(t)$ and $(0,t)$ agree,
and the total error is bounded by
$n_T M x^{-1+\varepsilon}x(\log x+C_d+K_o)$.
For $\xi$ trivial on $H$ this latter error is zero. For the principal
frequency the entire cost per term is $C_d$. For each discarded frequency
use $\Re(\xi(e_1(t))G_\xi(y_t))\ge-|G_\xi(y_t)|$ and the increment
bound to get a lower bound $v_\xi-(\log(x+1)+C_d+|C_E|\log x)$.
These are exactly the three cases of [D564](../../units/D564.md).

For a threshold independent of the host, let $s=x^{1/4}$,
$e=x^\varepsilon$ and
$$
 A_1=5+C_d+|K_o|+|M|(4+C_d+|K_o|)+4|C_E|.
$$
Since $\log x\le4s$, $\log(x+1)\le5s$ and $1\le s,e$, each of the
three per-character costs per $t$ is at most $A_1 s e$ (the coefficient
error uses $x^{-1+\varepsilon}x=e$). Increase the threshold until
$|M|A_1\le s$. Summing over the band costs at most $n_Ts^2e$,
so the factor four in the following bound is slack: the cost is at most $4n_Tx^{1/2+\varepsilon}$. Taking real parts gives
$$
 n_T(G-4x^{1/2+\varepsilon})
 \le \sum_{t\in TT}\Re\sum_{\xi\in\mathcal A}
                 \xi(e_1(t))G_\xi(y_t).
$$

## Finite-group average and B09

Put $f=|\Phi|=2n$. For each $u\in A_0$ compare the frozen sum
$T(u,t)$ of Lemma 3.9 with one column of $\mathrm{De}$.
At a thick
place $b\le w\le b+\eta+1$ and $a_t\le(x+1)b$, so replacing its
weighted value by the frozen one costs at most $3(x+1)(\eta+1)$.
At a thin place $0<w\le2b'$. Since $a_t\ge(x-1)b$,
$b'X'\le xb$ and $x\ge3$, one has $a_t/w\ge X'/3$.
Thinness therefore bounds $w|G_\xi(a_t/w)|$ by $a_t\theta\le (x+1)b\theta$. There are at most $f$ places and $2f$ characters,
each with unit-modulus Fourier coefficient and normalization $1/f$.
The sum of absolute errors is at most
$$
 2f\big[3(x+1)(\eta+1)+(x+1)b\theta\big]\le 2b/x
$$
by the two cost inequalities in [B09](../../units/B09.md).
The balance identity now gives
$\Re T(u,t)\le\mathrm{ASK}_{t,j}-\Re\mathrm{MAIN}_{t,j}+2b/x$
for every column $j$. Thus if $\mathrm{gap}(u)\le E$ on $A_0$, then
$\sum_{t,j}\Re T(u,t)\le E+2n_Tmb/x$ on $A_0$.
`CharacterBalanceMoves.Th`, `th_le`,
`LandauTheorems/ChCore.lean:16–20,75–152`;
`CharacterBalanceMoves.core`, `LandauTheorems/ChCore.lean:283–320`.

For $s\in T_2\subset A_0$, sum $\xi(-e_1(s+u-t))$ over $u\in A_0$.
Its value is $|A_0|\xi(e_1(t))$ if $\xi\in\mathcal A$, since
$-e_1(s+u-t)=e_1(t)+(0,-s)+(0,-u)$.
Otherwise choose $u'\in A_0$ with $\xi(0,u')\ne1$; translating the
sum by $u'$ multiplies it by $\xi(0,-u')$, hence the sum vanishes.
Consequently the average of $T(u,t)$ over $A_0$ equals
$b(\delta_2/2)\sum_{\xi\in\mathcal A}\xi(e_1(t))G_\xi(y_t)$:
the factor is $bn_2/f$. Sum over all $t$ and the $m$ columns and apply
the preceding character lower bound. Since $|A_0|>0$, the result is
$$
    n_T m b(\delta_2/2)(G-4x^{1/2+\varepsilon})\le E+2n_Tmb/x .
$$
With $E=x^{C\varepsilon}B$, $C\ge0$, the size-window calculation
in Lemma 3.10 now gives $G\le x^{1/2+(C+3)\varepsilon}$.
Its hypotheses are precisely `RestSize`, the upper rank and
lower $k$ inequalities, $x\ge3$, $26\le x^{3\varepsilon/8}$, and the
sign and cardinality conditions ([D563](../../units/D563.md), [D566](../../units/D566.md)).
Adding $\Sigma_A$ proves B09. The threshold precedes the choice of
$H,TT,T_2$, the weights, and $m$.

`LandauTheorems/ChCore.lean:28–73`;
`CharacterBalanceMoves.core`, `LandauTheorems/ChCore.lean:322–338`;
`Deduction.ch_core`, `LandauTheorems/ChCore.lean:343–370,419–442`.

## The four terms after division by the number of columns

Here is the numerical implication used in B09. Write $n=|H|$, $t=|TT|$,
$r=|T_2|$, $\delta=r/n$, $Q=tmb$, and $G=G_m^A-\Sigma_A$. Put
$X=x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, $Y=x^{1/2+13\varepsilon/8}$ and $P=x^{C\varepsilon}$.
The bracket before normalization is
$$
 \mathrm{Br}=t a_E(1+m^2/k)
       +m\left(2nmbx^\varepsilon+
       \frac{r k b x^\varepsilon}{n^2 x^{-\varepsilon}}\right).
$$
Here $r=|T_2|$ is a cardinality local to this calculation.
The size record in [D566](../../units/D566.md) gives, with $x\ge3$, $\varepsilon>0$, $C\ge0$, $b>0$ and $n>0$,
$$
\begin{gathered}
0\le a_E\le2xb,\qquad n/t\le 2x^{\varepsilon/8},\qquad
x^{-\varepsilon}\le\delta\le1,\\
x^{1/2-\varepsilon}\le m\le x^{1/2+\varepsilon/2},\qquad
xm\le k\le n^2 x^{1/2-\varepsilon}.
\end{gathered}
$$
In particular $t,m,k,Q$ are positive. More precisely the original inequality
$t\ge n x^{-\varepsilon/8}/2$ gives positivity of $t$ before taking
reciprocals. Assume $26\le x^{3\varepsilon/8}$, as is possible for
every fixed $\varepsilon>0$.
See `SizeWindows`, `GrowthBoundGivesRiemannHypothesis.lean:109–123`,
and `size_windows_split`, `ChainSlopeWindows/PChain.lean:23–26`.

**Size bound, [D563](../../units/D563.md).** 
If $\mathrm{Err}\le P\,\mathrm{Br}$ for the source bracket and the
character average gives
$$
Q\,\frac{\delta}{2}(G-4X)\le\mathrm{Err}+2Q/x,
$$
then $G\le x^{1/2+(C+3)\varepsilon}$.

**Proof.** 
Expand $\mathrm{Br}$ and divide its four summands by $Q$.
For the first, the lower rank bound gives $x/m\le X$; for the
third the upper rank bound controls the extra factor of $m$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{a_E}{mb}&\le2x/m\le2Y,\\
\frac{a_E m}{bk}&\le2xm/k\le2Y,\\
2(n/t)m x^\varepsilon
 &\le4x^{\varepsilon/8+1/2+\varepsilon/2+\varepsilon}=4Y,\\
\frac{r k}{n^2t}x^{2\varepsilon}
 &\le(n/t)x^{1/2+\varepsilon}\le2x^{1/2+9\varepsilon/8}\le2Y .
\end{aligned}
$$
These are precisely the terms of `errorBracketSizeWindows`
(`ErrorFormsWeakWindowsFalse.lean:133–136`);
the four estimates occur as `SZ.T1`–`SZ.T4`
in `LipschitzWeightAndMinimum.lean:31–113`.
Consequently $\mathrm{Err}/Q\le 10PY$. Since $2/x\le1\le PY$, division by
$Q$ gives $\delta(G-4X)\le22PY$. Divide by $\delta>0$ and use
$\delta^{-1}\le x^\varepsilon$. Both $X$ and $PYx^\varepsilon$ are at
most $Z=x^{1/2+(C+21/8)\varepsilon}$ (the second equals $Z$), so
$G\le4X+22PYx^\varepsilon\le26Z$. Finally $26Z\le x^{3\varepsilon/8}Z$
is the asserted bound. See `proposition_size_bound`,
`LipschitzWeightAndMinimum.lean:507–592`.

The factor $b\delta_2/2$ comes from $bn_2/(2n)$ after averaging a normalized sum, before the column count. Both the cancellation of nontrivial frequencies and the common, host-independent threshold are needed.

## The bound before taking characters

At one scale let $H$ be the finite additive group of the reference frame,
$A_0\le H$, $TT\subset H$, $T_2\subset A_0$ and
$n=|H|$, $n_T=|TT|$, $n_2=|T_2|$, $\delta_2=n_2/n$.
Write $\mathrm{gap}(u)$ for the sum of
$\mathrm{ASK}-\Re\mathrm{MAIN}$ over $t\in TT$ and $1\le j\le m$
at translate $u$. Let $B$ be the four-term bracket in
[B09](../../units/B09.md), with $a_E$ the lattice parameter $a$.

**Lattice inputs for the gap.** 
Under the eleven hypotheses in [P021](../../units/P021.md), at each lattice unit $v$,
$\mathrm{ASK}(v)-\mathrm{Main}(v)\le\mathrm{ErrX5at}(v)$.
Under the error windows and $\mathrm{LargeX}$,
$\mathrm{ErrX5at}(v)\le x^{(e_{\rm Div}+e_{\rm Loss}+3)\varepsilon} \mathrm{ErrText}$ ([D567](../../units/D567.md)). The actual bounds for $B_0,N_c$
and the required size and identification hypotheses are specified in

## Derivation of the gap bound, B10

For $v$ mapping to $u$, replace the top and place indices by the given
bijections with $TT$ and $\Phi$. The summands of the lattice main term
then have exactly the recorded $a_t$, $w_{u,j}$, Euler constant and
$\Re\ell(\chi_C)$, so the sum is $\sum_{t,j}\Re\mathrm{MAIN}_{t,j}$.
The identification of the ask term gives $\sum_{t,j}\mathrm{ASK}_{t,j}$.
Their difference is $\mathrm{gap}(u)$ ([D569](../../units/D569.md)).
Now $\mathrm{ErrText}=n_Ta_E(1+m^2/k)+m(B_0+N_c)$.
Insert $B_0\le2nmbx^\varepsilon$ and
$N_c\le n_2 k b x^\varepsilon/(n^2x^{-\varepsilon})$.
All multipliers are nonnegative, so $\mathrm{ErrText}\le B$.
Combining the two inequalities in 3.3 gives
$$
    \mathrm{gap}(u)\le x^{(e_{\rm Div}+e_{\rm Loss}+3)\varepsilon}B.
$$
Every $u\in A_0$ has a preimage by the coverage clause in
`CoreAtH`; this transfers the bound to the entire subgroup.
`Deduction.ch_top_main_eq`, `LandauTheorems/ChTop.lean:11–35`;
`Deduction.ch_top`, `LandauTheorems/ChTop.lean:37–72`;
`CoreAtH`, `PrimitiveCosets/CoreAtH.lean:29–41`.

# A single eventual threshold for the whole tied family

**Pending independent review** (`pending_review`). Full local implication under the assumptions of [P017](../../units/P017.md). Source edition: paper v4, §3.1, pp. 10–20.

The one-scale estimate is available for every eligible host once its fixed constants have been chosen. Its derivation is included with B08 (one scale), B10 (lattice gap) and B09 (finite average and numerical bounds). In v4 the statement begins on p. 10, the one-scale proof ends on p. 19, and the family argument appears on p. 20. The separate numerical lemma finishes on p. 21.

[B08](../../units/B08.md) · [B09](../../units/B09.md) · [B10](../../units/B10.md) · [P021](../../units/P021.md) · [P018](../../units/P018.md)

**P017, family window estimate.** 
Fix a level $\Lambda$, real $e_D,e_L$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Let $F$ be a
family of type `FamP` at $\varepsilon$ with the uniform explicit-formula hypothesis
$\mathrm{EFamC}(\Lambda,F)$. Suppose that there exist $K,c_{HH},e_K,C_L,x_0$
such that, for every $x\ge x_0$ in $\mathrm{Win}(F)$,
$\mathrm{ChainTied}(F;e_D,e_L,K,c_{HH},e_K,C_L,x)$ holds.
Then there exists $X$ such that on this same set for $x\ge X$,
$$
     \mathcal G_\Lambda(x)\le x^{1/2+(e_D+e_L+7)\varepsilon}.
$$
Here $\mathcal G_\Lambda$ is the real weighted prime sum of
v4 Definition 6.19 (p. 77). The estimate is one-sided.

`UpperTheory.Comparison₂.level_gm_le_on_family_scales`,
`LevelGmLeOnFamilyScales.lean:28–30`;
`Formalism.HC.ChebyshevInequalityOnWindows`,
`TotientGaloisClasses/TopWin.lean:23–28`.

## Family quantifiers and proof of Proposition 3.1

Unpack $\mathrm{EFamC}$ to obtain $C_E,x_E$ such that every member at
each $x\ge x_E$ satisfies $\mathrm{EAtH}$ with $C_E$. Fix the five
eventual-tiedness witnesses of the proposition. Let $X$ be the maximum
of $x_0,x_E$ and the B08 threshold for these constants. For $x\in \mathrm{Win}(F)$, $x\ge X$, unpack $\mathrm{ChainTied}$ at this $x$.
Use its reference member $i_0$, take the translation map to be the identity
on its frame group, and use the word fibre of the assigned member
$\mathrm{pt}(u)$ at each $u$. Every frame element is its own preimage, so coverage holds on the whole frame group and in particular on $A_0$. The arithmetic tie's
test-set membership equation and the family's common $TT$ image identify
$TT$ with the reference host's $TT$ by injectivity of the frame coordinate.
Its digit description at translate $0$ expresses each $s\in T_2$ as a digit
in the cyclic subgroup $A_0$. The same tie supplies the compatible
$\ell$. Restrict the weight bounds and cutoff from all translates to
$A_0$, and retain the two bijections, identities, lattice size and error
bounds, thin scales, costs and remaining-size bounds. These are exactly

# D014 · Inertia and Frobenius for the arithmetic of a fixed host

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

**Full · pending_review.** This proof concerns the local arithmetic of an axial host already given on a frame. The [unit statement](../../units/D014.md) is in manuscript v3, Appendix G.16, p. 160. The [v4 proof of Lemma 3.7](D014_v4.md), §3.1, pp. 15–16, gives the same seven fields. Its consumers include the [host window estimate](../../units/B08.md). All source locators below use the Lean commit in the unit record.

## The conductor and the sign

Write $Q$ for the host’s positive integer $\mathrm{QS}$, $q$ for its distinguished prime and $d$ for its other distinguished prime. The conductor is $N=Qqd$, with $d$ prime to $Qq$ and $d\equiv3\bmod 4$. Write $S$ for the prime factors of $Qq$. The arithmetic record is obtained by sending a unit modulo $N$ through the host Artin map and then into the additive group of the frame. Call this composite $r$. Its sign coordinate determines the predicate $\mathrm{InPhi}$. A multiplicative sign of $+1$ corresponds to additive sign zero. The required exceptional inertia element is the particular frame element $\mathrm{sgc0}$. The seven fields of the conclusion specify both the prime set and the local images. See the definition of **HostFactsS** in `SplitInertia.lean:14-22` and the construction **hostFactsS_pf** in `hostFactsS.lean:44-57`.

Here is the sign test used twice below. If a unit $u$ is congruent to $k$ modulo $d$, its sign in the host is the Jacobi symbol $(k/d)$. Indeed the host’s Artin-character identity gives the symbol of a residue representative of $u$, and congruence modulo $d$ replaces that representative by $k$. Hence $(k/d)=1$ implies $\mathrm{InPhi}(r(u))$. The arithmetic sign is a unit, so equality of its underlying integers suffices before passing to additive notation. This proves **inPhi_of_jac**, `hostFactsS.lean:7-15`.

## Away from the distinguished prime

The elementary fields hold at once. The host makes $d$ prime, $2\mid Q$, $q$ prime and $d\nmid Qq$. Positivity gives $Qq\ne0$, so $2,q\in S$ and $d\notin S$. If $p$ is prime, $p\notin S$ and $p\ne d$, then $p\nmid N$. Indeed a divisor of $Qqd$ divides $Qq$ or the prime $d$. At an unramified prime the local unit subgroup used to define inertia is trivial. Membership in inertia means being $r(u)$ for a unit in this subgroup. Thus $u=1$ and $r(u)=0$. This proves triviality of the whole additive inertia subgroup. The relevant calls are **unramified_spec** and **mem_inertia_iff** in `hostFactsS.lean:49-70`.

Now let $p\in S$. The prime $d$ divides the prime-to-$p$ part of $N$, since $d\mid N$ and $p\ne d$. A $p$-local unit is $1$ modulo this part and hence modulo $d$. The sign test with $k=1$ puts its inertia image in $\mathrm{InPhi}$. The chosen Frobenius unit is congruent to $p$ modulo the same part. For $p=2$ the congruence $d\equiv7\bmod16$ gives $(2/d)=1$ by the supplementary law, the use of **jac_two_d**. For an odd $p\mid Q$, quadratic reciprocity gives $(p/d)=(-d/p)$ since $d\equiv3\bmod4$: the sign from interchanging $d,p$ is exactly $(-1/p)$. The host splitting law at $p$ gives $(-d/p)=1$. For $p=q$, the congruence $q\equiv3\bmod8$ makes $q$ odd and the stipulated $(-d/q)=1$ gives the same conclusion. These are all the primes dividing $Qq$. The sign test with $k=p$ gives the Frobenius assertion. See **jac_of_dvd**, **d_dvd_ordCompl** and **frobUnit_modEq** in `hostFactsS.lean:17-38` and `hostFactsS.lean:71-82`.

## Equality of the inertia image at $d$

A $d$-local unit is $1$ modulo $Qq$. The host condition **art_d** restricts its Artin image to the identity or the distinguished involution. Passing through the frame identification sends these to $0$ and $\mathrm{sgc0}$ respectively. This proves one inclusion. The identity local unit realizes $0$. To obtain the other element, choose by the Chinese remainder theorem a unit $u$ satisfying

$$
u\equiv 1\pmod{Qq},\qquad u\equiv-1\pmod d.
$$

Both residues are units and the moduli are coprime. The first congruence gives local membership. The second gives Artin sign $(-1/d)=-1$, since $d\equiv3\bmod4$. Thus the identity possibility in **art_d** is excluded, and the resulting image is exactly $\mathrm{sgc0}$. This proves the reverse inclusion. See **toE_iod'** and **hostFactsS_pf** in `hostFactsS.lean:40-42`, `hostFactsS.lean:83-105` and `hostFactsS.lean:106-125`.

Finally the small primes are the prime factors of $Q$. As $Qq\ne0$ and $q$ is prime, adjoining $q$ to that set gives exactly $S$. Replacing $S$ by this equal finite set in the seven proven fields proves **UpperTheory.Comparison₂.hostFactsS**, `hostFactsS.lean:127-136`.

**Referee check.** Trace the two different uses of congruence. The $p$-Frobenius unit for $p\mid Qq$ reduces to $p$ at $d$. The witness for exceptional inertia instead reduces to $-1$ there. Interchanging the witnesses would lose the proof that the prescribed involution actually occurs.

# D014 · Inertia and Frobenius at the exceptional host primes

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

The pinned source paths below use the root `src/`. The proof is adapted from the project’s manuscript v4 and is **pending_review**. Manuscript v4, §3.1, printed pp. 15–16. [Unit card](../../units/D014.md) · [Mathematical editions](../../data/editions.json).

- **A6** `UpperTheory.Comparison₂.hostFactsS`, `Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/PrimitiveCosets/hostFactsS.lean:127–136`.

**Exceptional primes of the same host, D014**

For every frame and every host satisfying $\mathrm{HostAx}$ on it, put $Q=\mathrm{QS}$, $N=Qqd$, $S=\{q\}\cup\{p:p\mid Q,\ p\text{ prime}\}$. Let $I_p,F_p$ denote the inertia subgroup and Frobenius element of its arithmetic datum. Then $d$ is prime, $2,q\in S$, $d\notin S$, and, for prime $p$,

$$

 \begin{array}{ll}
 p\notin S\cup\{d\}:& I_p=\{0\},\\
 p\in S:& I_p\subseteq\Phi,\quad F_p\in\Phi,\\
 p=d:& I_d=\{0,s_0\},\qquad s_0=((1,0),0).
 \end{array}

$$

Here $\Phi$ consists of the elements with first binary coordinate zero.

`Deduction.CH.HostFactsS`, `DedekindLFunctions/SplitInertia.lean:14–22`; `UpperTheory.Comparison₂.hostFactsS`, `PrimitiveCosets/hostFactsS.lean:127–136`; `Formalism.D5.InPhi`, `PartnersToFactorsAt.lean:20`.

**Proof.**

The host has $q,d$ prime, $q\equiv3\pmod8$, $d\equiv7\pmod{16}$, $(\frac{-d}{q})=1$, $2\mid Q$, and $(Q,qd)=1$. The two residues modulo eight are distinct, so $q\ne d$. Since $Qq\ne0$, $S$ is exactly the set of prime divisors of $Qq$; this proves the four assertions on $d,2,q,S$. For prime $p$, write $N^{(p)}=N/p^{v_p(N)}$. The inertia subgroup is the image under $r=\operatorname{toE}\circ\operatorname{art}$ (in additive coordinates) of the units $u$ modulo $N$ with $u\equiv1\pmod{N^{(p)}}$. The Frobenius unit has residues $p$ modulo $N^{(p)}$ and $1$ modulo $p^{v_p(N)}$; these specify one unit by the Chinese remainder theorem. Its image is $F_p$. By the host character law, the first binary coordinate of $r(u)$ is zero precisely when the Jacobi symbol $(\frac{u}{d})$ is $+1$: this coordinate encodes the second multiplicative sign of $\operatorname{art}(u)$. `HostHyp`, `FrobeniusOrbits/Statement.lean:13–14`; `HostRaw`, `HostDer.art_ch`, `ConjEMemHostFIff.lean:12–52,99`; `recH`, `arith`, `PrimitiveCosets/RecH.lean:10–23`; `mem_localUnits_iff`, `frobUnit_modEq`, `mem_inertia_iff`, `GaloisMapComplexConjugation.lean:33–40,86–89,123–128`.

If $p\notin S\cup\{d\}$, then $p\nmid N$, hence $N^{(p)}=N$. Only the identity unit contributes to inertia, giving $I_p=\{0\}$. If $p\in S$, then $d\mid N^{(p)}$. Every inertia unit is $1$ modulo $d$ and hence has positive symbol. The symbol of the Frobenius unit is $(\frac p d)$. For $p=2$ this is $+1$ since $d\equiv7\pmod8$. For odd $p\mid Qq$, quadratic reciprocity and $d\equiv3\pmod4$ give $(\frac p d)=(\frac{-d}p)$: the reciprocity sign $(-1)^{(p-1)/2}$ equals $(\frac{-1}p)$. The right side is $+1$ by the host's splitting hypothesis for odd $p\mid Q$, and by its defining condition for $p=q$. This proves both inclusions in $\Phi$. `jacobi_neg_recip`, `TotientGaloisClasses/HostFacts.lean:15–24`; `jac_two_d`, `GaloisMapComplexConjugation.lean:290–295`; `inPhi_of_jac`, `jac_of_dvd`, `d_dvd_ordCompl`, `PrimitiveCosets/hostFactsS.lean:7–38`.

Finally $N^{(d)}=Qq$, since $d\nmid Qq$. If $u\equiv1\pmod{Qq}$, the host law $\operatorname{art}_d$ restricts its Artin image to $1$ or the frame involution $\mathrm{iod}$, which map to $0$ and $s_0$. The identity unit realizes $0$. The coprime moduli $Qq,d$ admit a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $Qq$ and $-1$ modulo $d$. This is an inertia unit whose symbol is $(\frac{-1}{d})=-1$; its Artin image cannot be the identity, so it realizes $s_0$. This proves equality at $d$ and exhausts the fields of $\mathrm{HostFactsS}$. `HostRaw.art_d`, `ConjEMemHostFIff.lean:45–46`; `toE_bij`, `PrimitiveCosets/ToEBij.lean:37–39,67–71`; `exists_unit_crt`, `GaloisMapComplexConjugation.lean:47–61`; `hostFactsS_pf`, `PrimitiveCosets/hostFactsS.lean:44–125`.

## Point for the reviewer

Check the chosen local unit at d and its sign after the binary coordinates in the frame are exchanged.

Assume a fixed host satisfying its frame axioms, $x>0$, the explicit-formula datum $\mathrm{EAtH}(\Lambda,H,TT,x,\varepsilon,C_E)$, and a logarithmic-derivative function $\ell$ compatible with the matched primitive characters. Here $TT$ is the set of selected places and $n_T=|TT|$.

Put $E_0=(\mathbb Z/2)^2$, $s_0=((1,0),0)$, $e_1(t)=s_0+(0,t)$ and $\mathcal A=\{\xi\in\widehat{E_0\times H}:\xi(0,A_0)=1\}$. The character sum at $y$ is denoted by $G_\xi(y)$. Write $K'$ for the kept subset, $o=\Lambda.o$, $c=(3o+1)^{-1}$, $M=4o$, $K_o=\sum_{\psi\in\Lambda.\mathrm{KEPT}}|(L'/L)(1,\psi)|$ with the stated convention for the logarithmic derivative at one.

Using weight one on characters trivial on $H$ and $c$ on the others, the finite host sum equals $\mathcal G_\Lambda(y)$ at every real $y$.

Let $P$ be the host modulus and let $\mathrm{art}:(\mathbb Z/P)^\times \to\phi.\mathrm{GG}$ be its surjective Artin map. The frame isomorphism $\iota_E:\phi.\mathrm{GG}\to E_0\times H$ sends $((a,b),m)$ to $(\sigma(b),\sigma(a),\iota^{-1}m)$, where $\sigma(+1)=0$, $\sigma(-1)=1$. Its inverse decodes the two signs in reverse order and uses $\iota$ on the last coordinate. Hence $\theta_\xi=\xi\circ\iota_E$ runs once through the host characters. Let $p_\xi$ be the primitive character inducing $\theta_\xi\circ\mathrm{art}$ on units. If $p_\xi=p_{\xi'}$, inducing both to $P$ gives equal unit values. Surjectivity first of $\mathrm{art}$ and then of $\iota_E$ gives $\xi=\xi'$. The zero additive character corresponds to the principal primitive character $\mathbf1$. By definition $K'=\{\xi:p_\xi\in\Lambda.\mathrm{KEPT}\}$. The kept clause of $\mathrm{EAtH}$ represents each member of $\Lambda.\mathrm{KEPT}$ by a host character trivial on $\tau_1(A_0)$ and on $\mathrm{iod}$. Consequently $K'\to\Lambda.\mathrm{KEPT}$ is bijective. By injectivity these two triviality properties hold for every $\theta_\xi$ with $\xi\in K'$. In additive coordinates they read $\xi(0,A_0)=1$ and $\xi(s_0)=1$. See `toE`, `recH` (`PrimitiveCosets/RecH.lean:10–23`), `chr_bij`, `prim_inj` and `EAtH` (`ChrBij.lean:25–29`, `PrimInj.lean:6–27`, `ExplicitFormulaErrorOfHostConditions.lean:144–151`).

We check that the two prime sums use the same character even at primes dividing $P$. For a prime power $p^i$ with $i>0$, the local factor in `primVal` is the character average on $i\operatorname{Frob}_p+I_p$. If $\xi$ is nontrivial on $I_p$, translation by an element with value different from one annihilates the average. In this case $p$ divides the conductor of $p_\xi$ and its Dirichlet value is zero. Indeed, by the Chinese remainder theorem the kernel of reduction to the prime-to-$p$ part of $P$ is the local factor $(\mathbb Z/p^{v_p(P)}\mathbb Z)^\times$, and its image is $I_p$. Killing that kernel is equivalent to factoring the character through the prime-to-$p$ modulus. If it is killed, the average is $\xi(\operatorname{Frob}_p)^i$; the Frobenius unit is congruent to $p$ modulo that prime-to-$p$ modulus and hence modulo the conductor. Thus in both cases the factor is $p_\xi(p)^i$. Products over prime powers give equality at every positive integer. For $\xi\ne0$, compatibility of $\ell$ now gives $\ell(\xi)=(L'/L)(1,p_\xi)$ in the convention of the manuscript. The two sums run over $1\le n\le\lfloor y\rfloor$ and $(y/n-1)_+=y/n-1$ on this range; it is empty for $y<1$. The principal terms have the same explicit correction. Thus $G_\xi(y)=g_{p_\xi}(y)$ for every real $y$, with $g_{\mathbf1}=G$ the level's principal function. See `primitive_value_primitive` and `cosetMean_eq_primitive` (`ChainSlopeWindows/GaloisMapComplexConjugation.lean:86–96,129–150,209–245`), `prim_read` and `Gz_eq` (`PrimitiveCosets/PrimRead.lean:25–97`, `PrimitiveCosets/GzEq.lean:6–50`).

For a kept $\xi$ trivial on all of $H$, the host character kills the $H$ factor and $\mathrm{iod}=((1,-1),1)$. It factors through the first sign. Its value at $((-1,1),1)$ has square one, so it is the trivial character or the sign character $\phi.\mathrm{psC}$. Both restrictions are conversely trivial on $H$. The first has level weight one. If the second is kept, the exceptional-character clause of $\mathrm{EAtH}$ identifies its primitive character with $\Lambda.\mathrm{psK}$ and gives it weight one: an absent $\mathrm{psK}$ explicitly precludes keeping $\phi.\mathrm{psC}$. Every other kept character has nontrivial $H$ restriction and is neither principal nor exceptional by injectivity, so both weights are $c$. Reindex the weighted sum over $K'$ by $\xi\mapsto p_\xi$, then separate $\mathbf1$ from the remaining terms. This proves $G_m^A(y)=\mathcal G_\Lambda(y)$, D547 (`gmA_eq_triv`, `gmA_eq`, `PrimitiveCosets/GmAEq.lean:16–59,61–149`).

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

## A8 · Prime-power balance

**Prime powers in one column.**

Write $U=(\mathbb Z/2)^2\times H$ and $\Phi=\{g=((g_1,g_2),h):g_1=0\}$. Thus $|U|=2f$ with $f=|\Phi|=2|H|$. The character $\chi_C(g)=(-1)^{g_1}$ distinguishes the two cosets of $\Phi$. For $t\in H$ set $P_t(g)=((1,1),0)+g+((0,0),t)$. Translation by this fixed element interchanges $\Phi$ and its complement. The data at a prime $p$ are a subgroup $I_p\le U$ and an element $F_p\in U$. Write $0\in\widehat U$ for the character identically one and $[z]_+=\max(z,0)$ for real $z$. The host hypothesis here is `Deduction.CH.HostFactsS` (D014): a finite set $S$ contains $2,q_1$, and $d$ is a prime outside $S$. For primes $p\notin S\cup\{d\}$, $I_p=\{0\}$; for $p\in S$, $I_p\subset\Phi$ and $F_p\in\Phi$; and $I_d=\{0,((1,0),0)\}$. `DedekindLFunctions/SplitInertia.lean:14–22`; `InPhi`, `cconj`, `topPl`, `ThickAverageLoss/PartnersToFactorsAt.lean:20–29`; `partner`, `chC`, `ArithData`, `SizeWindowBrackets/FirstPrimeNeSecondPrime.lean:19–42`.

**Exact prime and character balance**

Take the host just specified, any function $\ell:\widehat U\to\mathbb C$, $a>0$, $t\in H$, a width function $w:U\to\mathbb R$ positive on $\Phi$, and $N\in\mathbb N$ with $a/w(\rho)\le N$ for every $\rho\in\Phi$. Put $W_g=w(P_t(g))$ for $g\notin\Phi$ and $h(v,g)=[a/v-W_g]_+$. Here $p$ is called inert if it is prime, $p\notin\{2,q_1,d\}$ and $F_p\notin\Phi$. Then, as an identity in $\mathbb C$, $\mathrm{ASK}-\mathrm{MAIN}=\mathrm{De}$, where the three quantities are

$$

\begin{aligned}
 \mathrm{ASK}={}&
 2\sum_{\substack{p\le N\\p\ {\rm inert}}}
  (\log p)\!\sum_{\substack{1\le i\le N\\iF_p\notin\Phi}}h(p^i,iF_p)
 + (\log d)\sum_{i=1}^N
  \sum_{\substack{g\notin\Phi\\g-iF_d\in I_d}} h(d^i,g),\\
 \mathrm{MAIN}={}& a\left(\log a-1-\gamma+\ell(\chi_C)
           -\frac1f\sum_{\rho\in\Phi}\log w(\rho)\right),\\
 \mathrm{De}={}&\frac1f\sum_{g\notin\Phi}\sum_{\xi\in\widehat U}
      \overline{\xi(g)}\,W_g G_\xi(a/W_g).
\end{aligned}

$$

Here $G_\xi$ is the centered character sum defined in the proof and $\gamma$ is Euler's constant.

**Proof.**

For $n\ge1$ let $v_\xi(n)$ be the product over $p\mid n$ of the means of $\xi$ on $\operatorname{ord}_p(n)F_p+I_p$. The empty product is one, and $v_0(n)=1$. At a prime power $p^i$, $i\ge1$, the product has just one factor. Finite Fourier orthogonality thus gives

$$

 \frac1f\sum_{\xi\in\widehat U}\overline{\xi(g)}v_\xi(p^i)
 =\frac{1}{f|I_p|}\sum_{z\in I_p}\sum_{\xi\in\widehat U}
                         \xi(iF_p+z-g)
 =\frac{2}{|I_p|}\,\mathbf 1_{g-iF_p\in I_p}.

$$

Indeed the inner sum at zero is $|U|$: decompose $U$ into cyclic factors, on each of which the characters are the roots of unity of the corresponding order. At a nonzero element one of the cyclic geometric sums vanishes. At most one $z$ has $iF_p+z-g=0$. This explains both the inertia divisor and the factor $2$. See `cosetMean`, `primVal`, `FirstPrimeNeSecondPrime.lean:61–66`; `orthogonality_ramified`, `ChainSlopeWindows/StronglyIrreducible.lean:311–317`.

Consider the finite Fourier sum

$$

 J=\frac1f\sum_{g\notin\Phi}\sum_{\xi\in\widehat U}\overline{\xi(g)}
       \sum_{n=1}^N\Lambda(n)v_\xi(n)h(n,g).

$$

Only prime powers $n=p^i$ contribute, with $\Lambda(n)=\log p$. Since $P_t(g)\in\Phi$, $a/W_g\le N$. Thus $h(p^i,g)=0$ whenever $p^i>N$, and one can sum over $p\le N$ and $1\le i\le N$. Evaluate the character sum using the preceding identity.

- For $p\in S$, both $F_p$ and $I_p$ lie in $\Phi$, so no $g\notin\Phi$ contributes.

- For $p\notin S\cup\{d\}$, only $g=iF_p$ can contribute, with coefficient $2$. If $F_p\in\Phi$, all its multiples lie in $\Phi$. Otherwise $p$ is inert (since $2,q_1\in S$) and precisely the exponents with $iF_p\notin\Phi$ give the first term of $\mathrm{ASK}$.

- For $p=d$, the coefficient on $iF_d+I_d$ is $2/2=1$. Intersect this coset with $U\setminus\Phi$ to get the second term of $\mathrm{ASK}$. If $d>N$, every $d^i>N$ and the written term vanishes.

Evaluate $J$ in the other order. Put

$$

 L_\xi(y)=\sum_{1\le n\le y}\Lambda(n)v_\xi(n)(y/n-1).

$$

Then $G_0(y)=L_0(y)-y\log y+(1+\gamma)y$ and, for $\xi\ne0$, $G_\xi(y)=L_\xi(y)+y\ell(\xi)$. Fix $g\notin\Phi$, put $W=W_g$ and $y=a/W$. $$

 \begin{cases}
 a\log a-a\log W-(1+\gamma)a,&\xi=0,\\
 -a\ell(\xi),&\xi\ne0.
 \end{cases}

$$

$$

  =\mathbf 1_{\xi=0}-\mathbf 1_{\xi=\chi_C}.

$$

Thus the nontrivial-character correction is $+a\ell(\chi_C)$, with the plus sign coming from the two minus signs. Together the corrections give exactly $\mathrm{MAIN}$. ## A10 · Fixed-width thick places

**The thick part of the place sum at fixed width**

Write $g=((\alpha,\beta),h)\in E_0\times H$ and $\Phi=\{g:\alpha=0\}$. Let

$$

 \begin{gathered}
 c_{\rm conj}=((1,1),0),\qquad
 \operatorname{topPl}(t)=((0,0),t),\qquad
 \operatorname{thickPl}(s)=((0,1),s),\\
 P_t(g)=c_{\rm conj}+g+\operatorname{topPl}(t)
       =((1+\alpha,1+\beta),h+t).
 \end{gathered}

$$

This $P_t$ is `partner`. The condition `IsThickAt`$(T_2,u,\rho)$ means $\rho=\operatorname{thickPl}(s+u)$ for some $s\in T_2$. Fix $a=a_t$, $b>0$, and a column with weights $w$. $$

 T(u,t)=\frac{b}{|\Phi|}\sum_{s\in T_2}
      \sum_{\xi\in\widehat{E_0\times H}}
        \xi(-e_1(s+u-t))\,G_\xi(a/b).

$$

**Proof.**

The first sign of $g+\operatorname{topPl}(t)$ is $\alpha$, so the translated complement of $\Phi$ is exactly the original complement. There $\alpha=1$ and $P_t(g)=((0,1+\beta),h+t)$ belongs to $\Phi$. Finite character values have modulus one, hence $\overline{\xi(g)}=\xi(-g)$. Inserting these two equalities in the definition of $\mathrm{De}$ gives

$$

 \Re\mathrm{De}=\Re\left(\frac{1}{|\Phi|}
 \sum_{g+\operatorname{topPl}(t)\notin\Phi}\sum_\xi
 \xi(-g) w(P_t(g))\,G_\xi(a/w(P_t(g)))\right).

$$

# B04 · Extending cuspidal parameters and recovering the tame type

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

**Outlined · pending_review.** Fix the valuation above the finite place $w$ of a number field $E$, in the given algebraic closure. Put $K=E_w$. The task is to choose a single reciprocity map and one assignment on smooth irreducible classes of all ranks over $K$. All the laws, including the last one about inertia, must hold for that assignment. Manuscript v3, §5.4, p. 36 gives the [statement](../../units/B04.md). The [theta and geometric construction](../../units/B03.md) uses a local parameter of this type to express its compatibility away from the coefficient prime.

## From cuspidals to all irreducible classes

First choose an Artin map $a$. The construction **artEx** starts with local Artin existence. It also proves uniqueness by mapping both candidates through a common global Artin law, then using injectivity of the local idele comparison. The proof of B04 retains $a$ and its Artin property. It discards this additional uniqueness witness. Keeping the same $a$ throughout determines which character is used when a representation or a parameter is twisted. See `ArtEx.lean:7-15` and `LocalCentralUnits/RecTExists.lean:20-26`.

Next, **cuspEx** supplies an assignment $r$ with the cuspidal laws for this $a$. Its construction makes the scope of the theorem important. On the good cuspidal classes it uses **goodMap**. On the complement it uses a chosen auxiliary parameter of the right rank with a real norm twist. For a cuspidal class outside the good class the rank is at least two, since rank one is good. The argument checks irreducibility and dimension separately on the two branches. For the inflated types in the final law the depth and local-field conditions put the class back on the good branch. Thus the strong character and type compatibility has a definite place to enter the proof. See `CuspEx.lean:168-193`, `CuspEx.lean:258-266`.

Extend $r$ by multisegments. Exhaustion supplies a multisegment for each irreducible class $x$. To each segment attach its prescribed special Weil–Deligne summand, built from the parameter of the first cuspidal class with the segment shift. Sum over the multisegment. If another list presents $x$ as the same Langlands quotient, the classification gives equality of the two multisets. The direct sum is invariant under reordering, so both lists give the same parameter $r_c(x)$. For cuspidal $x$ one may use the one-term list consisting of the singleton segment of $x$. Its shift is $(1-1)/2=0$, the special block has length one, and summing the resulting parameter with the zero parameter returns $r(x)$. These are precisely the existence and restriction conclusions of **exists_isLExt**, `LanglandsExtensionUniqueOnCuspidal.lean:34-56`.

## Which compatibilities survive extension?

The returned record uses the equality $r_c=r$ on cuspidal classes in three distinct places. It gives the rank-one formula from the law for characters. Applied to every segment head, it puts the multisegment formula into the convention using $r_c$ itself. It also transports irreducibility for every cuspidal class. The **extDim** and **extTw** inputs handle dimensions, central characters and twists. Real norm twists are unconditional. For a general character twist the proof chooses a presenting multisegment, uses the goodness of the support on each head and twists the corresponding individual parameters. The theorem asserts the absolute central-character comparison on all classes and the full central-character identity on good support. See `LocalCentralUnits/RecTExists.lean:27-57` and `RcTwOfSegments.lean:36-57`.

Duality and injectivity on good support enter as the separate **extDual** and **extInj** inputs. For the depth conclusion, consider a wild inertia element. At a principal-congruence fixed vector, the depth property descends to the cuspidals in the support. On a good constituent of rank $j$, the characteristic polynomial on wild inertia is $(X-1)^j$. The product formula for the support and additivity of its ranks give $(X-1)^{\dim r_c(x)}$. The tameness criterion in **extDepth** converts this identity to the claimed property. See `LocalCentralUnits/RecTExists.lean:39-44` and `ExtDepth.lean:11-34`.

## Returning the inertia polynomial

The type condition applies over a base completion continuously isomorphic to $\mathbb Q_p$. At the chosen place $w'$ upstairs the prime is unramified, expressed by $p\notin (w')^2$, and the residue field has cardinality $p^n$ for $n>0$. One uses a surjective residue map with kernel $w'$, a regular residue-field character and an inflated cuspidal type with the prescribed elliptic character values. These are hypotheses of **TypeLaw**, `NonGaloisDescent/RecTExists.lean:34-52`. The source uses **typeIff** to pass between a law expressed by a residue map on inertia and the law using an Artin unit over that extension. In the direction used here it constructs the extension record and its reduction map, restricts inertia to the base, and identifies the resulting residue unit with the prescribed one. This is why matching the element in the exponent is part of the argument. See `TypeIff.lean:46-57`.

Finally inflation of the stipulated type gives cuspidality of the class in question. Replace $r_c(x)$ by $r(x)$ at precisely this class. The cuspidal type law supplies zero monodromy and the characteristic polynomial with roots $\vartheta(z^{p^j})$ for $0\le j<n$ at the specified inertia element. Both clauses concern the same parameter. This last specialization is **recTExists**, `LocalCentralUnits/RecTExists.lean:58-66`.

**Referee check.** The construction of the good cuspidal map and its tame-type law remains a substantial input. Check where inflation supplies cuspidality and where the local depth and field hypotheses force the good branch. The unrestricted auxiliary choices in the other branch carry fewer character compatibilities.

## Read the quantifiers before supplying the row

The conclusion is the universal half-plane assertion $H$ used by [P009](../../units/P009.md). P010 obtains it by applying the row-to-$H$ implication [P011](../../units/P011.md) to an inhabitant of its row hypothesis. This is the exact application in `UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/MainConclusion.lean:10–11`). Paper v3, §6.10, p. 56 identifies that supplier. Its type and especially its compatibility across places explain why this specialization has mathematical content upstream. [Manuscript excerpt](P010.tex)

Fix a CM number field $E$, an algebraic closure, a coefficient prime $\ell$ and an identification of its algebraic coefficient field with $\mathbb C$. Fix a positive rank $a$, a cuspidal datum $\pi$ and a character over the maximal real subfield. Assume the regular algebraic and polarized-pair conditions. The required row provides a Galois representation of rank $a$, an integer weight and a family of multisets of Hodge–Tate weights indexed by embeddings of $E$. The output includes one proof of the compatibility record for these choices. The order of the universal inputs and the joint existence clause are in `UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0b` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/TypeConditions/WeightsConjBis.lean:69–73`).

That record requires continuity and semisimplicity. Away from $\ell$ it compares the local Weil–Deligne data of the representation with the parameter of the local component. It specifies the weights and their transformation under complex conjugation. Its last field gives the indicated conditions above $\ell$ when the requisite local bridge and tied data are present. Quantifying independently over places after choosing a single representation is essential. Independent choices of representations at the different places would not fill the record. The six fields are in `UpperTheory.GalStar.PropsB` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/TypeConditions/WeightsConjBis.lean:54–67`). The particular parameter relation is the one named in `UpperTheory.Gal.Int.recT` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/IntegralStructures/Development.lean:18–18`).

## Follow the geometric supplier

The term passed to P011 is `UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisLocalGlobalStrong_recParameter` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/IntegralStructures/RowSrc.lean:6–6`). It calls the theorem turning a theta-lift input into the row and supplies the named theta-lift result `UpperTheory.TP.K.tLiftK` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/ThetaParseval/ThetaKernels/TLiftK.lean:4–5`). The conversion `UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisRepresentations_of_thetaLift` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/IntegralStructures/GaloisRepresentationsOfThetaLift.lean:6–6`) also calls the geometric existence result for the prescribed geometric input. Thus a referee checking existence at this point needs to inspect both sources. An asserted local compatibility on its own cannot create the global representation.

Follow the conversion one level further. Given the geometric and theta-lift inputs, `UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisLocalGlobal_of_geometry_lift` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/IntegralStructures/Development.lean:27–28`) builds a seed for the odd-level argument from the geometry and obtains a congruence input from the weight result. It passes these with the lift to `UpperTheory.Gal.Int.coreAll_of` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/IntegralStructures/Development.lean:20–22`). The latter brings together the descent, closed-trace and limiting steps to build a common core record. The next map `UpperTheory.Gal.Int.rest` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/IntegralStructures/Development.lean:24–25`) uses this core for the underlying row and for the spherical and Iwahori compatibility statements. The code explicitly derives the Iwahori input from the spherical compatibility on the same core. This is where an attempted derivation from independently chosen local data would have to supply an identification.

## Weaken the row and discharge the implication

What these steps initially produce is the stronger row `Row0`. The weaker version needed at P011 is obtained by `UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisLocalGlobalStrong_of_geometry_lift` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/IntegralStructures/Development.lean:30–31`). Unfold `UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0.row0b` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/Foundations/GaloisRepresentations/TypeConditions/WeightsConjBis.lean:84–86`). For each choice of $E,\ell,a,\pi$ and polarization, extract $r$, its weight and its embedding-indexed multisets from the strong row. Return the same three witnesses. The operation on their properties forgets some of the stronger conditions and restricts the remaining tests. No fresh representation is chosen. The result therefore has exactly the parameter dependence required above.

Finally specialize `UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter_of_row` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/MainConclusion.lean:7–8`) to this supplied inhabitant. Its output has the same predicate $H$ as P010, so the last step is function application. This outline follows the construction down to its named geometric, theta and local-global inputs. It provides no independent proof of those existence and comparison results, or of the Selmer-window construction used inside P011.

**First point for review.** The source obtains one representation with the entire local compatibility record. Independently justifying this simultaneous existence from the geometric and theta-lift inputs is the first substantive gap in this outline.

# W08 · Summing the Case I Selmer lengths over primes and characters

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

**Outlined · pending_review.** For a primitive $\chi$ the bound chooses $C$ and two prime thresholds $r_1,r_2$ before the host. Fix a sufficiently large host $h$ of character $\chi$ with $q_1,d$ exceeding both primes, modulus $N$, and $0<e<t$. Let $T$ be any finite set of odd primes satisfying Case I ($\ell\notin B_\chi$ and $\ell-1\nmid2e$). At each prime choose its permitted coefficient ring $O_\ell$. The target includes finiteness of every localization length and the collective bound
$$
  \sum_{\ell\in T}\log\ell\sum_{\psi\in X_h(O_\ell,e)}v_\ell(\psi,e)\le(Nt)^C .
$$
Here $v_\ell$ denotes the normalized real length, after ruling out infinite length. The independence of $C$ from the size of $T$ is essential for [W13](../../units/W13.md). See paper v3 §5.44, p. 51, and v4 §5.44, p. 68. [Original statement](W08.tex). `CountI` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/AutomorphicVarieties/HeightAndVanishing/Counts.lean:53-58`).

Start with the automorphic package $H'$, one witness for [W05](../../units/W05.md), the two-twist Kato vanishing of [W07](../../units/W07.md), and the rank-three automorphy input for unramified coefficients. The cohomological package is specialized to the rank-$n$ field of $H'$ with that very cohomology witness. The linked unramified endpoint, adjoint lifting, first and second rigidity and even-level admissibility are then applied to compatible data. The three algebraic inputs are the two graded length comparisons and the additional algebraic lemma supplied by this route. For one eligible character the finite-length and trace-difference bound is first proved in an unramified coefficient model. The prime-to-$\ell$ order allows a representative there with the same values inside $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$. The pinned proof compares the good-data predicate, the normalized lengths and the twisted character values at the chosen Galois element and its inverse. This permits application of the unramified automorphy input. The integer used later in the sum must control characters in all the coefficient models selected by the reader. ## Turn local trace comparisons into a simultaneous orbit bound

Fix the imaginary quadratic field chosen from $\chi$, a kernel $H\subset(\mathbb Z/N)^\times$, and a good test prime $p$. The rank-three automorphic counting input is applied to all complex characters with that kernel. Their root-of-unity values and stability under coefficient conjugation supply the hypotheses of the counting input. It produces a nonzero integer with controlled logarithmic size and divisibility at the good coefficient primes. The proof chooses a place over $p$ and a Frobenius there and compares the complex and $\ell$-adic character orbits by an actual bijection. The one-character valuation inequalities can consequently be summed against the valuation of this same integer. `propGK_of_numberU3U_of_oneCharU` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/AutomorphicVarieties/ModularityArgument/ThresholdArguments/DenseThresholdCases/FPropGKU.lean:118-145`). `propGK_of_numberU3U_of_oneCharU` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/AutomorphicVarieties/ModularityArgument/ThresholdArguments/DenseThresholdCases/FPropGKU.lean:146-172`).

  2c_5\,\varphi([(\mathbb Z/N)^\times:H])\,[N(e+1)]^A

# W11 · A uniform class-group rank bound in every cyclotomic layer

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

$$
d_\ell(F)=\big|\mathrm{Cl}(F)/\mathrm{Cl}(F)^\ell\big|.
$$

Since the quotient has exponent dividing $\ell$, this bounds its dimension as an $\mathbb F_\ell$-vector space. The next consumer, [W12](../../units/W12.md), needs uniformity in the layer. Choose a cyclotomic field containing a copy of $K$, using the abelian-extension input of the source. Factor its conductor as $\ell^a f_0$ with $\ell\nmid f_0$. Set
$$
 f=f_0(\ell+1),\qquad D=f\ell^a .
$$
This harmless enlargement ensures $f>1$ and $(f,\ell)=1$. For a proposed tower threshold $n_0$ and any input layer $n$, put $m=n+a+n_0$. The embedding construction supplies $K'\subset L$ with $L$ a model of the cyclotomic field of conductor $f\ell^m$ over $\mathbb Q$. It works for the actual input model of $K'$, using its cyclotomic algebra structure. `embed` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/AutomorphicVarieties/GaloisLibrary/FerreroWashingtonIndex/EmbedDeg.lean:16-53`).

Here is the degree comparison that makes this maneuver uniform. The absolute degree of $L$ is $\varphi(f\ell^m)$, while the primitive root in $K'$ gives $[K':\mathbb Q]\ge\varphi(\ell^n)$. By multiplicativity and the prime-power totient inequality,
$$
 \varphi(f\ell^m)\le f\ell^{a+n_0}\varphi(\ell^n).
$$
Dividing the tower-degree identity by the positive number $\varphi(\ell^n)$ gives $[L:K']\le D\ell^{n_0}$. Even $n=0$ is covered. In particular the intersection of the difference subgroup for complex conjugation with the $\ell$-torsion is bounded by $B_0^N$, with $B_0,N$ independent of the layer. `cyc` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/AutomorphicVarieties/GaloisLibrary/FerreroWashingtonIndex/FerreroWashington.lean:18-33`). `cyc` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/AutomorphicVarieties/GaloisLibrary/FerreroWashingtonIndex/FerreroWashington.lean:42-55`). `cyc` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/AutomorphicVarieties/GaloisLibrary/FerreroWashingtonIndex/FerreroWashington.lean:77-90`).

# T17 · Why the small-section volume bounds the top intersection

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

**Outlined · pending_review.** Read this alongside [the statement and v3 locator](../../units/T17.md). The argument has two dimension cases. In the arithmetic curve case one can see directly how an additive error in a count disappears. In higher dimensions the geometric step is a comparison with ample perturbations.

## Fix the actual inequality

Write $P$ for the multihomogeneous vanishing ideal of a finite collection of coordinate blocks $y$ in a field. Assume that $P$ presents an arithmetic variety of dimension $D+1$, the presentation by $y$ is birational, and $I$ satisfies the intersection-system axioms. Fix a Hermitian line $A$, invariant under complex conjugation and semipositive relative to an ideal $P_0\subseteq P$. Its multidegree is nef on fibres. Its generic nef condition tests nonnegativity of geometric degree on arithmetic subvarieties of dimension two. Define $Q$ to be the source's small-section predicate for $(P,y,A)$ and $L_k$ its degree-$k$ chart lattice. The target is

$$
T=I_P(A^{D+1})\ \le\ \operatorname{arVolP}(Q,L,1,D).
$$

The parameter $1$ means we take the normalized counts along all positive integer powers. The related Hilbert–Samuel convergence statement assumes nonnegative heights of arithmetic curves and asks for a limit. Here we need an upper bound on $T$ by a limsup, using the given lattice, for every admissible $I$. The two statements occur next to each other. Source: `MoriwakiBigStatement` (`MoriwakiSt.lean:29–36`) and `MoriwakiHSStatement` (`MoriwakiSt.lean:18–27`); the generic nef predicate is defined just above them.

## Positive relative dimension

For $D\ge1$, split according to the sign of the generic degree of the multidegree of $A$. If it is positive, the data form the nef-and-big tuple required by the small-section lower estimate: take in order $P_0\subseteq P$, relative semipositivity, conjugation invariance, fibre nefness, and positivity of generic degree. Its characteristic-zero hypothesis follows here from horizontality. Indeed, a natural number vanishing in the coefficient field would give a constant polynomial in $P$. The contraction of a horizontal ideal to the integers is zero, forcing that natural number to be zero. Applying the positive-degree estimate gives precisely the displayed inequality for the original $Q,L$. Source: `charZero_of_isHorizontal` (`CharZeroOfIsHorizontal.lean:12–21`), `G6.StatementB` (`StatementsArith.lean:395–400`) and `ArithmeticVolumeBig.proof` (`CharZeroOfIsHorizontal.lean:23–28`).

If the degree fails to be positive, the remaining comparison accepts the weak inequality “generic degree at most zero.” This alternative matters: applying the positive-degree estimate a second time would require a missing hypothesis. In the construction of the second estimate, the auxiliary nef-plus-ample degree bound enters the shift of the line, bounded-height points enter the separation of sections, and lattice finiteness is used in passing from separated sections to a count. Shifted volume control, the polynomial identities for the shifted intersection and shifted degree, and the ample counting result feed the nonpositive-degree argument. Its output has the original unshifted line and chart lattice, so either branch proves the same inequality. These are named geometric inputs to this outline. Source: `hsChain` (`HSChain.lean:258–274`), especially the construction of the two final estimates, and `ArithmeticVolumeBig.Statement` (`StatementsArith.lean:404–410`), `ArithmeticVolumeBig.proof` (`CharZeroOfIsHorizontal.lean:23–28`).

## Arithmetic dimension one

For $D=0$ set $c_k$ equal to the logarithmic small-section count in $L_k$. The curve counting result gives a constant $C$ with $kT-C\le c_k$ for all $k\ge1$. Here the underlying construction proceeds from control of the index of the integral lattice and a box count on its number-field realization. The chart lattice is shown full for that count; replacing it by all elements of the ambient field would lose the comparison. The proof also applies the packing estimate to the chart lattice through its inclusion in the normalized lattice. It gives an upper bound of the form $c_k\le C'(k+1)$. Nonnegativity of the count makes $C'\ge0$. Source: `CurveCountLower.Statement` (`StatementsCurveCountLower.lean:9–16`), `hsChain` (`HSChain.lean:293–303`), `MoriwakiBigCurve.proof` (`PMoriwakiBigCurve.lean:15–47`) and `chartLat_le_chartLatNm` (`PMoriwakiBigCurve.lean:11–13`).

The normalization in dimension zero is $k^{0+1}/(0+1)!=k$. For $k\ge1$, $c_k/k\le2C'$, so the sequence is bounded above on the tail in the ordinary real line. Fix $\eta>0$ and take $k$ large enough that $C\le k\eta$. Division of the lower estimate by $k$ gives $T-\eta\le c_k/k$ for every such $k$. Thus the limsup is at least $T-\eta$ for every $\eta>0$, and letting $\eta$ decrease gives $T\le\operatorname{arVolP}(Q,L,1,0)$. This passes only to the limsup and uses the same $Q,L$ as the target. Source: `MoriwakiBigCurve.proof` (`PMoriwakiBigCurve.lean:15–47`), lines 24–47, and `MoriwakiBigCurve.Statement` (`StatementsMoriwakiBigCurve.lean:13–20`).

## Common inputs and review boundary

The dimension split now exhausts the natural numbers. The positive-dimensional comparison in this application does not consume the separately supplied generic-nef proof; the curve interface accepts it. The compiled assembly takes precisely the volume-big and curve components of a five-part package. It obtains resolution, an arithmetic intersection-system theorem from Poincaré–Lelong and that same resolution, and the dense bounded-height input. The resulting statement still quantifies over the particular admissible intersection system $I$ fixed at the outset. Source: `MoriwakiBig.of_found` (`MoriwakiBig.lean:11–16`), `moriwakiBig_of_classicalTheorems` (`HSChain.lean:365–370`), `arith_intersection_system_of_poincare_lelong` (`ArithIntersectionSystemOfPoincareLelongStatement.lean:11–12`) and `moriwakiBig_outright` (`Outright.lean:9–11`).

A referee should first examine the nonpositive-degree estimate and its use of dense bounded-height points to separate small sections on the shifted line. That is where a change of lattice or semipositivity hypothesis could invalidate transfer to the limit. The short wrapper alone does not establish this geometric estimate on paper. The surrounding covolume argument and its other inputs are indexed in [T15](../../units/T15.md).

# P001 · From a right-half-plane bound to the zeta zero line

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

**pending_review** · Reading outline against Lean commit `40e56bab026552e089d7afcfeff08d2defb9c005`. [Unit card](../../units/P001.md)

## The input to the reduction

Fix a zero $s$ of the Riemann zeta function. The public predicate also assumes $s\ne1$ and excludes $s=-2(n+1)$ for each natural number $n$. Its conclusion is $\Re s=1/2$. The two zeta exports share the same proof term. The route for P001 uses the Mathlib predicate itself, whereas P002 spells the predicate out. The public declaration is `riemannHypothesis` (`Main.lean:4–4`), its immediate supplier is `rhOfAll` (`Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean:9–9`), and the explicit quantifiers appear in `RiemannZetaZerosOnLine` (`Statements.lean:3–4`). The manuscript places the two formulations side by side on p. 54. [v3 statement](P001.tex) · [Companion P002](../../units/P002.md)

Write $H$ for nonvanishing of every Dirichlet $L$-function in $\Re s>1/2$ subject to the principal-character exception. The substantive analytic argument at this export is an implication from $H$. The separate supplier of $H$ is [P009](../../units/P009.md). Keeping $H$ as an input isolates exactly what the reflection calculation needs.

## Specialize the character and choose the point of reflection

Take the character of modulus one. Every point in the right half-plane other than $1$ satisfies the second disjunct of $H$. The modulus-one identity equates its $L$-function with $\zeta$. We obtain a function assigning $\zeta(t)\ne0$ to every $t$ with $\Re t>1/2$ and $t\ne1$. No simplicity or isolation hypothesis on the zero enters this specialization. This is the entire call to $H$ in `Formalism.VW.rh_of_every` (`Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:29–32`).

Compare $\Re s$ with $1/2$. Equality gives the desired relation. A value strictly larger than $1/2$ contradicts $\zeta(s)=0$ directly. In the remaining case put $t=1-s$, so $\Re t>1/2$. The value $s=0$ would contradict $\zeta(0)=-1/2$. Consequently $t\ne1$. Also $t$ cannot be a nonpositive integer because it has positive real part. These observations both permit the functional equation at $t$ and place $t$ in the domain of the nonvanishing input. The case division and side conditions occur in lines 5–30 of `Formalism.VW.rh_of_right` (`Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRight.lean:5–62`).

## Exclude the vanishing of every factor

The functional equation at $t$ expresses $\zeta(1-t)=\zeta(s)$ as the product

$$
2(2\pi)^{-t}\,\Gamma(t)\,\cos(\pi t/2)\,\zeta(t).
$$

The base $2\pi$ of the complex power is nonzero. The gamma factor is nonzero because $\Re t>0$, and the modulus-one specialization already gives $\zeta(t)\ne0$. For the cosine, vanishing would give $t=2k+1$ for some integer $k$, and hence $s=-2k$. If $k<0$, this makes $s$ a positive even integer, contradicting $\Re s<1/2$. If $k=0$, it gives the zero argument already excluded. If $k>0$, then $k-1$ is nonnegative and $s=-2((k-1)+1)$ violates the public hypothesis. The pinned term converts $k-1$ to a natural number explicitly before invoking that hypothesis. These factors occupy lines 31–59 of `Formalism.VW.rh_of_right` (`Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/RhOfRight.lean:5–62`). Their nonzero product contradicts the original zero in its line 60.

Thus the displayed implication from $H$ supplies the zeta predicate, and the export reuses that implication with the particular term supplied by `allChi` (`Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean:7–7`). The outline leaves the construction of that term at its own card. A check of these lines can cover the modulus-one reduction, reflection and exceptional zeros while leaving the arithmetic source of the half-plane bound as a separate review obligation.

**First point for review.** The reflection step divides the cases at a negative even integer and at zero. Check the precise exclusion of each against the predicate passed to the public export.

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

## The exact assertion exported

Take a positive modulus $N$, a complex Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $N$ and a point $s$ with $\Re s>1/2$. The extra hypothesis is $\chi\ne1$ or $s\ne1$, where $1$ denotes the principal character at modulus $N$. Thus a nonprincipal character may be tested at $s=1$, and the principal character may be tested at every point allowed by the real-part condition except $s=1$. Either alternative is sufficient. The definition including the order of these binders is `DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf` (`Statements.lean:6–8`). The manuscript identifies this whole assertion with $H$. [Manuscript v3, §6.3, p. 55](P003.tex)

Unfolding `UpperTheory.EveryCharacter` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/EveryCharacter.lean:13–14`) gives the same positive-modulus instance, universal character and complex variable, the same two implications and the same function value in the conclusion. Therefore a term proving the internal predicate has exactly the type required by the public predicate after unfolding. This conversion explains the short proof term. The arithmetic entering its supplier can be seen in the following more detailed conditional reduction.

## Lift nonvanishing from the conductor

Suppose the primitive-character nonvanishing predicate is available. Let $M$ be the conductor of $\chi$ and let $\psi$ be the primitive character of modulus $M$ inducing $\chi$. The construction supplies a nonzero conductor, and applying the primitive hypothesis to the packaged character at $s$ gives $L(s,\psi)\ne0$. To use the change-of-level relation we must also have $\psi\ne1$ or $s\ne1$. If the public disjunction gives $s\ne1$, retain it. Otherwise use $\chi\ne1$. Were $\psi$ principal, changing it to level $N$ would again give the principal character. The change-of-level identity for $\psi$ would identify that character with $\chi$, a contradiction. These are the operations in lines 8–19 of `UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/Imprimitive.lean:5–35`).

The change-of-level formula now expresses $L(s,\chi)$ as $L(s,\psi)$ times a finite product of local factors of the form $1-\psi(p)p^{-s}$. Consider a prime appearing in this product. We have $p>1$ and $\Re s>0$. In particular,

$$
|\psi(p)p^{-s}|\le p^{-\Re s}<1 .
$$

The inequality uses the norm bound for a Dirichlet character, which also allows a zero character value at a nonunit. It uses the real-valued positive base $p$ in the norm formula for the complex power. If the local factor vanished, the product inside the absolute value would equal one, contradicting the strict inequality. Each factor is nonzero, so its finite product times $L(s,\psi)$ is nonzero. The pinned proof performs this argument prime by prime in lines 20–35 of `UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive` (`Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/CharacterBoxes/Imprimitive.lean:5–35`). An empty prime set contributes the multiplicative identity and already fits the product proof.

The use of $\Re s>1/2$ belongs to this upstream primitive result. The local Euler factors only require positivity of $\Re s$. This difference identifies which part of the calculation carries the difficult half-plane bound. [Primitive input P015](../../units/P015.md) · [Conditional passage P014](../../units/P014.md)

# P005 · Reflect a primitive zero across the middle of the strip

AI-written, AI cross-reviewed; no human sign-off; not a claim that RH is proved

**pending_review** · Reading outline against Lean commit `40e56bab026552e089d7afcfeff08d2defb9c005`. [Unit card](../../units/P005.md)

## Fix the character and isolate the input

Let $N>0$ and let $\chi$ be a primitive complex Dirichlet character of modulus $N$. We are given $0<\Re s<1$ and $L(s,\chi)=0$. The target is $\Re s=1/2$. The public definition places primitivity before the universal quantifier over $s$ in `PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine` (`Statements.lean:14–16`). The export `LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive` (`Main.lean:12–12`) uses `critAll` (`Supplements/Kernels/MainTheorems.lean:11–13`), the primitive reflection wrapper [P007](../../units/P007.md). The following argument explains the wrapper's exact use of the all-character half-plane statement $H$, supplied by [P009](../../units/P009.md). [Manuscript v3, §6.5, p. 55](P005.tex)

The strict strip bounds exclude $s=0$ and $s=1$. Suppose the real part differs from $1/2$. If $\Re s>1/2$, apply $H$ to $N,\chi,s$ using $s\ne1$ for the disjunction permitting nonvanishing. This contradicts the zero. When $\Re s<1/2$ we have to transport the zero to the other half of the strip. The strict alternatives and direct contradiction appear in lines 11–16 and 27 of `Formalism.VW.critLine` (`Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:11–27`).

## Pass to the completed function at the original point

Write $\Lambda(\chi,s)$ for the completed $L$-function. The source form of the identity at $s\ne0$ is $L(s,\chi)=\Lambda(\chi,s)/\gamma(\chi,s)$. In totalized field division a quotient can vanish if its denominator vanishes. To conclude that the numerator is zero, the proof checks the denominator. For an even character the gamma factor is $\Gamma_{\mathbb R}(s)$, and for an odd character it is $\Gamma_{\mathbb R}(s+1)$. The first argument has positive real part by the strip hypothesis. In the second case adding one keeps the real part positive. The respective gamma factors are therefore nonzero. These two cases are `Formalism.VW.gammaFactor_ne_zero` (`Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:6–9`), and lines 19–21 of `Formalism.VW.critLine` (`Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:11–27`) use the result to infer $\Lambda(\chi,s)=0$.

## Apply the functional equation in the needed direction

The inverse character is primitive because inversion preserves the conductor. Apply the primitive functional equation to $\chi^{-1}$ at $s$. Its left side is the completed function for the inverse character at $1-s$. Its right side contains the completed function for $(\chi^{-1})^{-1}=\chi$ at $s$, which has just been shown to vanish. Thus $\Lambda(\chi^{-1},1-s)=0$. The proof uses multiplication by a zero here and does not divide by a root number. The choice of inverse character and the simplification are in lines 17–23 of `Formalism.VW.critLine` (`Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:11–27`).

Set $t=1-s$. The original bound $\Re s<1$ gives $t\ne0$, so the ordinary-to-completed formula is available there as well. Its numerator is zero, which suffices to give $L(t,\chi^{-1})=0$. On the other hand $\Re t=1-\Re s>1/2$. We also have $t\ne1$ because $s\ne0$. Apply $H$ to $N,\chi^{-1},t$ with this latter alternative in its disjunction. The two conclusions contradict one another. The argument at $t$ is in lines 24–26 of `Formalism.VW.critLine` (`Formalism/GammaFactorNonvanishing/CritLine.lean:11–27`).

Both strict inequalities have been eliminated, so equality follows under $H$. The public Lean term uses the same $N$, character, point and strip hypotheses throughout the wrapper. No change to an inducing primitive character occurs on this path, since primitivity was supplied at the start. Obtaining $H$ uniformly in the modulus remains the separate arithmetic input to this local reflection argument. [Half-plane statement](../../units/P003.md)

**First point for review.** Check that the functional equation is used for the inverse character, and that the ordinary-to-completed quotient at the original point has nonzero denominator.
